spec.assertion: Structural: trigger hitCount count 120, target enemy, buff damageTakenPct 17.18 durationSec 5. Behavioral: every damageTakenPct buffApply is boss-held (casterIdx===null && targetIdx===null) at +17.18; emptying skill1 lowers EVERY firing unit's damage (fails under the nearest-wrong self/ally scoping, which would move only sakura); patching count 120->60 must raise activations >1.5x and raise team damage (fails if the trigger is not a landed-hit counter); patching durationSec 5->10 must raise team damage (fails if the window is already 10s or is round-counted); activation count must land in 8..30, the band the 120-round magazine + 81f reload allows over 180s (fails if the trigger counts pulls/intervals instead of landed hits). Inertness: shot and reload event counts unchanged vs skill1 removed.

No StatKey expresses incoming-healing scaling and v1 models no HP pool, so the line is unmodelable — it.skip documents it. Guarded by two live assertions: skill2 must contain NO heal/shield effect (the nearest-wrong mis-encode, which would fire crown-style on-recovery consumers every 60 landed hits — a large over-credit), and emptying skill2 must leave every unit's total byte-identical.

This is an ALLY defensive line; damageTakenPct is a BOSS-scoped stat, so encoding it on the enemy would apply a -14.97% team-wide damage CUT. Asserted by: no boss-held damageTakenPct event is negative or near 14.97, plus the byte-identical skill2-removal test. Fails under the nearest-wrong 'ally Damage Taken down = boss debuff' reading.

Structural: trigger burstCast (not fullBurstEnter — two Burst I units share the comp, so FB-enter keying would over-credit rotations liter cast), target alliesLowestHp count 2, heal ticks 10 intervalSec 1. Behavioral (TANDEM, the only observable a heal has at scope lock): team total with the burst > with the burst emptied, and > with ticks patched 10->1, because crown's on-recovery consumer is fed 10 times per cast rather than once. Non-vacuity gate first: a burstCast event naming sakura must exist. Inertness: burst-bucket damage-event count unchanged (the burst is pure sustain, no invented damage rider).

fixtures: controlComp('sakura-suzuhara', true) only — liter(B1) / crown(B2) / sakura(carry) / helm(B3); 7 hoisted 180s runs (base, skill1-removed, skill2-removed, burst-removed, skill1 durationSec->10, skill1 hitCount->60, burst heal ticks->1). crown is retained deliberately: her 'when recovery takes effect' trigger is the ONLY damage-visible consumer of a heal at scope lock (no HP pool, no recovery event kind), so it is the instrument that makes the burst line falsifiable. FIXTURE RISK, stated up front: sakura is a Burst I unit occupying the carry slot, so the comp holds TWO Burst I units and liter may win stage 1 on every rotation — the burst group therefore opens with an explicit non-vacuity assertion that localizes that failure instead of letting it masquerade as a modeling defect.
gaps: it.skip 'Incoming healing +15.18% for 10 sec' — no StatKey models incoming-healing scaling; v1 has no HP pool, so the line has no observable. Belongs in the override's `unmodeled`, not in a block.
it.skip 'Damage Taken -14.97% on allies for 10 sec' — damageTakenPct is boss-scoped; no ally-side damage-reduction primitive exists and the v1 boss deals no damage. Also belongs in `unmodeled`.

it.skip 'burst target set (2 lowest-HP allies vs all allies)' — the heal models no HP amount and alliesLowestHp resolves deterministically to the leftmost N at scope lock, so broadening the target set is unobservable unless the extra targets carry an on-recovery consumer.

HARNESS AMBIGUITY: the packet documents the override slot as BOTH `slot: Block[]` (OVERRIDE FILE SHAPE section) and `slot: { blocks: Block[] }` (harness cheat-sheet). Every reader/patcher in this file accepts either shape, and a shape-sanity test plus per-patch mutation counters (dur10Patched / count60Patched / ticks1Patched, each asserted > 0) prevent a counterfactual from silently no-opping on the wrong one.

HARNESS ASSUMPTION: the burstCast event's caster field name is undocumented, so the sakura-casts non-vacuity check matches the slug inside JSON.stringify(event). If burstCast carries only a numeric index, that single assertion will false-RED and should be re-keyed once the event shape is confirmed.
